topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks and tumor progression models.

topics.label: Proliferative signaling pathways and oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt/beta-catenin, and downstream cascades cause growth signal autonomy in cancer cells.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how mutations that arrest terminal differentiation contribute to tumor development in hematopoietic lineages and the intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 family regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how cancer cells evade programmed cell death by altering the balance between pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptotic proteins regulated by p53.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, cellular senescence, and p53 stress surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how telomere shortening and stress signaling enforce senescence and how cancer cells bypass these barriers to achieve replicative immortality.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and how Krebs cycle mutations generate oncometabolites that drive epigenetic deregulation.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and the angiogenic switch
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how expanding tumors stimulate new blood vessel growth to satisfy the oxygen and nutrient demands required for progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms, barriers, and genomic features of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the multi-step metastatic cascade, the physiological inefficiencies and seed-and-soil interactions governing colonization, and genomic characteristics like whole genome duplication.

topics.label: Conclusion and summary of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing remarks on the integration of cancer hallmarks and recommended reading.
